blocks.text: The reality of PR event planning

When you are coordinating press event logistics, your Mac becomes your command center. You jump between Gmail for correspondence, Google Docs for run-of-show documents, and Slack for team updates. The sheer volume of data makes it easy to lose track of small details. If you do not have a system, you spend more time searching for information than actually planning the event.
Why event coordination feels so hard

Most stress in PR comes from reactive workflows. You spend your day answering emails and Slack messages instead of focusing on the event strategy. This constant context switching kills your productivity. Research shows that 61% of experts cite expanded roles, including data and digital tasks, as a major contributor to their stress.

items: Last minute changes to guest lists.
Increasing technical demands for hybrid events.

blocks.text: You can improve your workflow without buying expensive enterprise software. Start by centralizing your communication. Use a single project management tool like Trello for visual tracking. Create a standard template for your run-of-show in Google Docs to ensure consistency across different events. Always document your contingency plans for common issues like vendor cancellations or tech failures.
Use the ⌘ space shortcut to open Spotlight and quickly find your event files. This saves you from hunting through Finder folders.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your workload

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay focused. When you are deep in an event planning document, you do not need to click away to check your calendar. Lazur keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the work.
